name: Editorial crew
description: A CrewAI crew researches a topic and writes an article, an editor agent polishes it under a house rule, and a person approves (or edits) it before it is marked ready to publish. Runs on CrewAI, which needs CrewAI installed on the server (make crewai).

channels.name: article
channels.description: The edited article the person reviews

channels.name: status
channels.description: Ready to publish, or sent back

agents.name: researcher
agents.goal: Find the facts {{ state.audience }} need to understand {{ state.topic }}
agents.backstory: You check every fact before you pass it on, and you say plainly when something is uncertain.

agents.name: writer
agents.goal: Write a clear, engaging article about {{ state.topic }} for {{ state.audience }}
agents.backstory: You write for busy readers: short sentences, concrete examples, no jargon.

tasks.description: Gather the key facts about {{ state.topic }} for {{ state.audience }}: what it is, why it matters now, and two concrete examples.
tasks.expected_output: Six to eight bullet points, each one fact with where it comes from

tasks.description: Write an article of about 600 words about {{ state.topic }} for {{ state.audience }}, using only the researched facts.
tasks.expected_output: A headline, then the article in Markdown with two or three short sections

config.goal: Make the article accurate, tight and easy to read for {{ state.audience }}
config.backstory: You edit for a careful publication. You cut what does not help the reader and keep the writer's voice.
config.expected_output: The edited article in Markdown, headline first
config.guardrail: The article starts with a headline, stays under 800 words, and contains no placeholder text such as [TODO] or [source].
